findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are never migrated to include the Clients schema
findings.body: `init` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP V2 before this change therefore retain a resource server with neither the new client scopes nor the `Clients` all-resource. Creating a client-targeted permission in such a realm fails when `getOrCreateResource` cannot find its scopes, and evaluating an unmaterialized client can subsequently dereference the missing all-resource in `ClientPermissionsV2`. Initialize or migrate the newly added scopes/resources when the client already exists.

findings.title: All-clients manage permission does not grant global view/list access
findings.body: `canView()` only recognizes default role-based view access and the global `view` scope; it does not recognize the global `manage` scope. Although `canView(ClientModel)` happens to get manage transitively through `canConfigure`, endpoints that gate listing or other global reads through `canView()`/`canList()` reject an administrator granted only `Clients/manage`. This also contradicts the expected manage-all behavior exercised later in the added test. Include the global manage permission in the global view decision.

findings.title: V2 role-mapping checks discard the existing manage-clients admin role
findings.body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate the new resource scope and never allow `AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS`. The established client permission evaluator grants a realm-management `manage-clients` administrator these operations, and the other V2 methods explicitly preserve that role. Enabling V2 will therefore cause existing manage-clients administrators to receive 403 responses when assigning client roles or editing composites unless separate V2 policies are created. Preserve the admin-role fast path in all three methods.

findings.title: Client deletion leaves V2 client authorization resources and policies orphaned
findings.body: The client-removal listener either skips handling when only the V2 feature is enabled (it tests the old `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature) or invokes `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Consequently, deleting a client with a materialized `Clients` resource does not remove that resource or its scope-permission policy references from the realm admin authorization server. Repeated client creation/deletion accumulates stale authorization data and exposes deleted client identifiers in permission administration; V2 needs explicit cleanup rather than the unsupported legacy per-client permission toggle.
